datasets: BPD Arrests 2026 (Open Baltimore ArcGIS export, data/arrests.csv)
311 Customer Service Requests 2026 (Open Baltimore ArcGIS export, data/requests_test.csv and 10K-row data/requests_small.csv)
concurrency_primitives: goroutine per dataset + sync.WaitGroup (main.go:65-96); per-file producer goroutine -> bounded chan []string (workers*4) -> runtime.NumCPU() worker goroutines -> bounded chan Record, closer goroutine, select on ctx.Done() (engine.go:147-329); Analyze/Report sequential
design_patterns: Pipeline (fetch -> parse -> analyze -> report), fan-out/fan-in worker pool, table-driven Strategy map of {title,score,keep} closures for the five analyses; no patterns named in README
questions: Q1 Highest arrest activity by 0.01-degree grid cell (single-dataset)
Q2 Highest 311 request volume by grid cell (single-dataset)
Q3 Grid cells with both arrests and infrastructure-type 311 requests
Q4 Combined arrests + 311 activity by grid cell
Q5 Unresolved (open-status) 311 requests by grid cell (single-dataset)
overview: Standard cmd/internal Go layout with a schema-tolerant CSV parser driven by a bounded-channel producer/worker-pool, a deterministic test, run.sh, and a colored interactive terminal menu. Nearly all logic (download, parse, aggregate, render) lives in one 593-line engine.go, aggregation is sequential, and the UI re-parses rendered report text by 'Q<n>:' prefixes. Code is clean and race-free but lightly commented.
stakeholder_value: Limited: no stakeholders are named, three of five questions are single-dataset rankings, and the two cross-dataset questions are co-location counts in anonymous 0.01-degree lat/lon cells rather than neighborhoods or rates. The honest caveats printed under each section are a plus, and the real-data run does surface genuine downtown-west hotspots, but a Mayor's Office reader would get coordinates, not actionable guidance.
issues: Default ./run.sh runs on 3-row synthetic fixtures; real data needs --real (network) or manual -arrests/-requests flags
README never mentions the bundled real CSVs (.gitignore excludes data/*.csv); 386 MB requests_test.csv appears to have shipped unintentionally
README's five-analysis list does not match the titles/order the program prints
No named stakeholders; Q1/Q2/Q5 single-dataset; Q3/Q4 are grid-cell co-counts
Aggregation and reporting are sequential; only parsing is parallel
ParseFile re-reads the entire CSV to count skipped rows; all records retained (948 MB RSS on full data)
engine.go is a single 593-line file spanning all stages; menu parses report text instead of structured results
Ends in interactive menu (exits cleanly on EOF, so scriptable)
rationale: Full build and run credit: clean build, passing tests, race-clean, and it processes 1.3 million real Open Baltimore rows in under five seconds. Real-data credit is 12 because both datasets are genuine and bundled but the default path is synthetic. Concurrency is partial (parse-only worker pool), and stakeholder credit is low because questions are mostly single-dataset grid-cell counts with no named stakeholder and a README/output mismatch. Total 75/100, C.
